meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis you gave it, and whether anyone heard Owen before you did.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing down November 2. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher said "like, being stuck," and that's your basis? Show me the note you wrote that day.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale. Put the October 15 outline and the essay in front of me, side by side. I'll read them myself.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

You still haven't shown me the outline, Hale. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, not a word in front of his class. Put the outline in front of me, and then we'll talk about Thursday at 8:15.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Today you acknowledged entering the zero before calling me, offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15, and said the new mark would replace the zero with nothing on his record. I still expect to see the October 15 outline and your November 2 note, and I require that nothing goes on Owen's record and that none of this happens in front of his class. You said I would have your offer in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, keeping it off his record and quiet, with nothing agreed and the rewrite offer not yet accepted.
What moved her: the October 15 outline arguing cowardice, which the essay never mentions, though she still hadn't seen it.
